question.problem:
Let $a=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$, $b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ and $c=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}].$ Find $2b+(-3a+c).$
$2b+(-3a+c)=\,\,$ {{field-1}}
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
To compute the result, we just need to perform the required operations with each component separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}2b+(-3a+c) & =2\,[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+(-3\,[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+([\begin{aligned}12 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
